protocol.purpose: Test physical cross-link following and signal stopping geometry using fresh cases and demand seeds; retain v1 as development diagnostics.
protocol.timeUnits: seconds for physical inputs and metrics; runtime ticks remain integers
developmentCases: all v1 held-out cases and demand seeds are now diagnostic development data

convergence.claim: Report measured trends; do not assume monotone convergence for every metric.

acceptanceCriteria.scope: Provisional numerical-equivalence targets for these matched-model experiments; separate from regression invariants and empirical validity.
acceptanceCriteria.headwayDefinition: Consecutive first-road exit event times within the same green interval; report count and match by vehicle pair.
acceptanceCriteria.queueDefinition: Vehicles on the approach with speed below 0.1 m/s, sampled at equal times; this is the halted queue, not every vehicle slowed by congestion.

stochasticReplications.stochasticSource: Independent seeded demand headway perturbations, shared exactly by both simulators; driver dynamics remain deterministic.
stochasticReplications.inferenceUnit: Scenario realization, not vehicles or time samples.
stochasticReplications.pairedMeanCi: Student t interval over independent per-seed HTC-minus-SUMO scenario means; n=5 uses t(4)=2.776445105.

empiricalValidation.status: unchanged exploratory pilot; v2 does not establish empirical validity
empiricalValidation.requirement: Use documented units, quality-control continuity and lane changes, separate initialization/calibration prefixes from prediction intervals, retain raw query/hash/license, and state environmental applicability. Field availability alone does not establish validation.

reportingRules: Retain every held-out result, including failures. Never widen thresholds after execution without a new protocol version and fresh validation set.
Freeze parameters before held-out execution. Store protocol SHA256 in each result.
Report signed bias, absolute error, distributions, coverage and invariant checks; do not align traces by fitted time shifts.
SUMO agreement does not substitute for empirical validation. Stochastic demand intervals do not quantify all epistemic uncertainty.
Separate wall-clock failures and unsupported scenarios from physical acceptance; retain and label all exclusions.
V1 diagnosed a missing leader across link boundaries. No car-following coefficients or acceptance limits may be tuned on v2 outputs.

interpretation: Controlled single-lane numerical equivalence to SUMO with protected movements; conditional on deterministic drivers and the frozen demand distribution. Does not establish empirical network validity.

initialV2Failure.reason: Link/16: requirement failed: unsolicited downstream MICRO boundary

excludedArtifacts.reason: Initial v2 execution: segmented Time Warp failed after a positive publication outlived its rolled-back subscription; 7 valid experiments and 1 engine failure are preserved. Traffic physics and frozen criteria unchanged; all validation repeated after guard repair.
Intermediate build before the stricter red-signal selector. Includes an exploratory zero-gap reference variant; final paired ablations use SUMO stop-line gap 1 m throughout.

remainingWork: Independent field following and queue-discharge validation with reserved data and justified acceptance thresholds.
Competing junction movements, shared conflict-area occupancy and multi-lane downstream selection.
Capacity-blocked handoff/spillback, including Node-waiting vehicles outside lane queues, needs separate representation and validation.
Extend observation beyond one connector and the next road for very short consecutive roads.
City-network geometry import and measured messaging/checkpoint cost at scale.
The current Krauss safe-speed expression remains a continuous stopping-distance approximation, not an exact copy of every SUMO discrete-model detail.
